clue.text: Make a speech — nothing standard

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
a standard is a rate, as in a rate of pay or performance

explanation.surface: An instruction to deliver a speech of no particular quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to declaim formally in front of an audience.

clue.text: Where children alone are cared for

definitions.text: Where children alone are cared for

parts.words: Where children alone are cared for
parts.note: children 'alone' are those left without parents, and the clue describes the institution that looks after them

explanation.surface: A description of a place where children left on their own are looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alone' looks like it means unsupervised, but here it means bereaved of both parents.
explanation.definitionFit: This institution houses and raises children whose parents have died.

clue.text: The plea of 13 across

parts.note: 13 across is the word for not being present, and the clue asks for the defence that claims one was elsewhere

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to the defence of not being there.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is ABSENCE: the accused pleads they were somewhere else when the crime happened.
explanation.definitionFit: In law this is the defence that the accused was elsewhere at the time of the offence.

clue.text: "Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts and "(Milton)

definitions.text: "Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts and "(Milton)

parts.words: "Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts and "(Milton)
parts.note: a quotation from Milton's Paradise Regained with its final word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A line of Milton praising ancient Athens, with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line in Paradise Regained runs 'Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts / And eloquence'; the solver fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens was famed for its orators, so Milton names fluent persuasive speech as one of its gifts.

clue.text: Royal insignia displayed in club restaurant

indicators.note: the royal letters are shown inside the golf club's name, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a brassie is an old name for a two-wood golf club
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher seen on postboxes and uniforms

explanation.surface: A royal emblem hung up in a members' club dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a social club; it is the golf club BRASSIE, an old name for a two-wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eating house.

clue.text: The original PBI on the way to Hannibal, perhaps

indicators.note: original means novel or newly made, so these letters are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way or road

explanation.surface: The first poor bloody infantry marching towards Hannibal's army.
explanation.walkthrough: PBI is old army slang for 'poor bloody infantry'. 'Hannibal' is not the Carthaginian general but the Handley Page HP42 airliner of that name, a 1930s two-winged aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Handley Page HP42 airliner named Hannibal was an aircraft with two sets of wings, one above the other.

clue.text: Having no beard was Len's disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes how something looks, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: Len, who used to wear a beard, shaved it off to go undercover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beard' is the botanical one: an awn is the bristle on an ear of barley, so this describes grass or grain without bristles.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the bristly 'beard' on a cereal head, and a plant lacking them is described this way.

clue.text: Spoken about quietly,'which is agreeable

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for spoken goes round the letter for quietly

parts.note: spoken means said
p, for piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Something whispered that turns out to be pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means savoury or pleasant to the taste, hence agreeable.

clue.text: The connection may be, clear — even though obscure

indicators.note: to obscure something is to muddle it, so these two words have their letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Perhaps the link between things is plain, even if it seems murky.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevance is the bearing or pertinence one thing has to another.

clue.text: The first mate trains each one

parts.note: Eve was Adam's partner, the first wife in Genesis
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a system of trains

explanation.surface: The chief officer of a ship drills every crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' looks nautical, but it is Eve, the first partner in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Every means all of a group taken individually, the same as each single one.

clue.text: Scurrilous writer on Pope's in trouble

indicators.note: trouble means disturb or stir up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: An anonymous slanderer targets the Pope, who is in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison pen writes malicious anonymous letters, scurrilous in content.

clue.text: This beats vegetables

explanation.surface: Something that beats vegetables, as if it outclasses them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beats' suggests defeating, but it is the throb of the heart; the second sense is beans, peas and lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart's rhythmic beat felt at the wrist is one sense; edible seeds of legumes such as lentils are the other.

clue.text: So long it takes to finish in gold!

indicators.note: in places the word for finish inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: An exclamation that it takes a long time to finish something in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' looks like a measure of time; it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: This French farewell is used in English much like goodbye.

clue.text: Abode very differently constructed in Wales.

indicators.note: built differently means these letters are assembled in another order

explanation.surface: A house built in an unusual style somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdovey is a seaside village in Gwynedd, on the Dyfi estuary in west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdovey is a coastal resort in west Wales.

clue.text: A lack of distraction

explanation.surface: A lack of anything to take one's mind off things.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is as in 'absence of mind', being distracted or inattentive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away or missing means a want of something; 'absence of mind' is inattention or abstraction.

clue.text: Place quickly fixed

parts.note: stead means place, as in 'in his stead'
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: Somewhere rapidly settled on.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means firmly set and unwavering.

clue.text: A minor Shakespearean character's gag

explanation.surface: A joke told by a bit-part player in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Justice Shallow's cousin, Justice Silence, appears in Henry IV Part 2. 'Gag' looks like a joke but is the verb to muzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A country justice in Henry IV Part 2 bears this name; to gag someone is to stop them speaking.

clue.text: For fun encourages growing things

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or a prank
spurs means urges on or encourages

explanation.surface: Something that promotes enjoyment of growing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspurs are garden flowers of the delphinium family, plants that grow.

clue.text: See about a stern resolution in serious fashion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the bishop's see goes round the other letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, a see

indicators.note: a resolution breaks a thing into new parts, so these letters are worked into another order

explanation.surface: Observe a firm resolve made in a serious way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a bishop's see; 'resolution' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means with sincere and grave intent.

clue.text: The Spanish and French house males in, the best environment

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: to house is to hold within, so the French word goes round the word for men

parts.note: et is the French for and
men are males

explanation.surface: Spanish and French houses where men live in ideal surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' goes with 'and', not with 'house': ET holds MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be 'in one's element' is to be in surroundings that suit one perfectly.

clue.text: Abuse one gets in some occupations

indicators.note: gets in means one letter enters the word for occupations

parts.note: trades are occupations
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who finds a job in certain lines of work and suffers insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches of denunciation, a form of verbal abuse.

clue.text: Stay in favour of support being given

parts.note: for means in favour of
to bear is to support a weight

explanation.surface: Remain in place in favour of the support being offered.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to hold back or refrain, the sense of stay as in stay one's hand.

clue.text: Punishes two ways -. that's cunning

parts.note: fines means punishes with a money penalty
S and E stand for the compass directions south and east, two ways to go

explanation.surface: Punishing in two different ways is the crafty approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is subtle skill or artfulness in handling a situation.

clue.text: Almost all exclude an outstanding star

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to debar is to exclude or bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone keeps out a celebrated star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' is a real star here: Aldebaran is the bright red eye of the constellation Taurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the brightest star in Taurus, prominent in the night sky.

clue.text: Moving music absorbs a holy man

indicators.note: absorbs means takes in, so the word for a tune encloses the saint

parts.note: an air is a tune or piece of music
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: Touching music takes in a saintly figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion.

clue.text: Game concealed in bog

annotationWithheld.why: Game concealed in bog (5): the scan prints 'bog', but IN in BOG gives BINOG, not BINGO, and no other reading of the words builds the answer

clue.text: Balance a small fish-plate

explanation.surface: Balancing a little dish of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish-plate' looks like a serving dish; it is one of the small plates covering a fish's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scales weigh things like a balance; each small horny plate on a fish's skin has the same name.

clue.text: A drink going round a second time

indicators.note: going round means the drink surrounds the second letter

parts.note: gin is a drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink served once more to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' puts GIN round A, and the first A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, on a further occasion.

clue.text: Mark Two

explanation.surface: A man's name followed by a number.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American author Samuel Clemens; the first definition is his surname with 'Mark'. 'Twain' is also an old word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Clemens wrote as Mark ____; the old word also means a pair.

clue.text: He argues a social worker should go after underworld set

indicators.note: should go after means the worker's letters come at the end, behind the others

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for it
put means set, as in put it down
an ant is a social insect that works in a colony

explanation.surface: A man says a social worker ought to follow a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is not a council employee but a social insect, and 'underworld set' looks like a gang but is two separate pieces; 'should go after' puts the insect last.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputant is a person engaged in an argument or debate.

clue.text: Turned up one's nose?

parts.note: the phrase usually means showed disdain, but read literally it describes a nose that tilts upwards

explanation.surface: Someone showing scorn at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up one's nose' means sneered, but the answer describes a snub nose.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word describes a nose with an upturned tip.

clue.text: A Scotsman in blue jeans and yellow' T-shirt

indicators.note: in means the name lies within these consecutive words

explanation.surface: A Scot dressed in denims and a yellow top.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy, short for Alexander, is a traditional Scottish name; it sits across 'jeanS AND Yellow', with sandy also meaning yellowish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy is the stock name for a Scot, a diminutive of Alexander.
